content: I am new contributor and would like to contribute to /Topos, what are ways to do so? Make ElementaryTopos.lean and PR?

Welcome and thanks for your interest in contributing to mathlib! For the theory of elementary topoi, you should coordinate with @Edward van de Meent who has done quite a bit of work on this in the past months. This area is very large, so it would help if you could give a more concrete description of what you have in mind.

More generally, I would recommend to discuss new contributions on Zulip first. In particular, if you plan to add new definitions. The hardest part about formalization is getting definitions right (mathlib does not even want to have every definition that exists in the literature!).

Thank you @Christian Merten ! I am learning the basics of topoi, logic, geometry, etc now, so I thought I could contribute whatever compiles. I don't yet know what formalisation make sense for mathlib?

Eg ElementaryTopos is cartesian closed with power object

class ElementaryTopos (C : Type u) [Category C] :=
 (fl : HasFiniteLimits C)
 (Ω : SubobjectClassifier C)
 (exp : ∀ A B, ExponentiableBy B A) -- A^B

I could formalise parts of textbooks, like for example by Goldblatt, or Johnstone, or MacLane, Moerdijk Fourman, …

How to get definitions right?

unfortunately for you, "whatever compiles" is not good for mathlib. Mathlib has a high standard of code quality and generality of proof, and the first thing that compiles definitely does not have those properties (as in, a person where those two coincide would be a genius prodigy of a kind of which i have never heard). I agree that formalizing as you learn a topic is a great way to improve your understanding, especially when that topic already exists in mathlib, but the code one produces will take a lot more work to be of the quality expected of mathlib.
Of course, if you're willing to put in the work, contributions are welcome.

As for what to contribute, I myself am planning to PR a proof of the fundamental theorem of topos theory, with the approach described in Jaap van Oosten's lecture notes for his course on topos theory. (i already have a proof in lean, now i just need to improve the code to mathlib quality. I'm in the process of PRing preliminaries.) This approach does not go through power objects, so perhaps you could contribute a definition/structure for such objects?
Thanks @Edward van de Meent! Why have this quality, and where to learn more about the purpose of it?

i don't know of sources which explain the purpose, but the main concerns (as i understand them) are

  • readability
  • conciseness
  • (re)usability (and as a consequence, generality)

You can find a lot of info about mathlib practices at contributing guide and linked pages therefrom

So maybe it's something like art of clean code and compatibility with the existing infrastructure.

The contributing guide seems useful, thank you @Edward van de Meent!

Why not have or have power object?
(you don't need to ping me every time you post in this convo)
It's hard enough to maintain, refactor, etc. the existing Mathlib code. It would be basically impossible to maintain whatever compiles. We'd quickly drown in technical debt.
